issues.message: CPML z-thickness is 0.6mm (6 cells), much thinner than xy-thickness 3.0mm. Absorbing performance may be asymmetric. Consider more z cells or fewer CPML layers.

dz_profile max adjacent cell ratio 5.000 exceeds the validated multi-band grading cap 1.4 (docs/guides/support_matrix.md, 'Multi-band graded mesh'). WHY: stability is unaffected (dt is the global min-cell CFL, sufficient on any tensor grid), but per-transition accuracy is witnessed only along z and only up to ratio 1.4 — the -54 dB reflection class at 30 cells/wavelength (it scales as (dz/lambda)^2), against -44 dB measured at ratio 2.0. COST: an unquantified reflection and grading-dispersion error at that transition. REMEDY: split it into ratio<=1.4 steps (e.g. rfx.smooth_grading) to stay inside the validated envelope, or accept it and say so in the report. STALE-IF: the support-matrix row raises the cap.

CPML reference reflections measured at 1 mm cells with the shipped CFS alpha (#1272, #1346): 6 layers: -38 dB at 2 GHz, -41 dB at 10 GHz, -32 dB at 30 GHz, -13 dB below 1 GHz. These reference values do not predict reflection on a different mesh or for UPML. Use at least 8 absorbing layers; 16 layers is the default recommendation.
